encode.name: english
encode.why: plain English — the basic form where spaces become metaspace

encode.name: english-long
encode.why: even with spaces the pre_tokenizer finds no split after normalization (one pre-token spans the whole input) — a length where merge rank / position ties are frequent
encode.text: Machine learning models trained on large corpora can generate text that is surprisingly coherent, but they still fail at arithmetic and long-horizon planning.

encode.name: japanese-long
encode.why: long text without spaces — one pre-token spans the whole input and a merge queue is needed (ADR 0084 decision 3)
encode.text: むかしむかし、あるところにおじいさんとおばあさんが住んでいました。おじいさんは山へしばかりに、おばあさんは川へせんたくに行きました。おばあさんが川でせんたくをしていると、大きな桃がどんぶらこどんぶらこと流れてきました。おばあさんはその桃を家に持ち帰り、おじいさんと二人で切ってみると、中から元気な男の子が飛び出しました。二人はたいそう喜んで、その子を桃太郎と名づけ、たいせつに育てることにしたのでした。

encode.name: cyrillic
encode.why: non-Latin, non-CJK (the boundary between in-vocabulary tokens and byte fallback falls elsewhere)
encode.text: Большая часть текста написана на русском языке.

encode.name: leading-space
encode.why: a leading space (metaspace comes first)

encode.name: trailing-space
encode.why: a trailing space (the right end of a merge is metaspace)

encode.name: double-space
encode.why: consecutive spaces (folded into the ▁▁ family of vocabulary entries)

encode.name: whitespace-run
encode.why: 30 spaces in a row — hits long metaspace entries (ranks near the top of the merges table)

encode.name: tab-newline
encode.why: whitespace the normalizer leaves alone (\t / \n do not become metaspace)

encode.name: newline-run
encode.why: 30 newlines in a row — the vocabulary has spellings that contain newlines (proof that a line-separated asset cannot work)

encode.name: digits
encode.why: digit strings — SPM-style vocabularies split them one digit at a time

encode.name: url
encode.why: long ASCII without spaces (a URL / base64 also becomes one pre-token spanning the whole input)

encode.name: mixed
encode.why: mixed Japanese and English — the vocabulary switches
encode.text: 1girl, 猫耳, ロングヘア, masterpiece

encode.name: emoji
encode.why: non-BMP + regional indicators + variation selector (hits byte_fallback)
encode.text: a cat 🐈 and a flag 🇯🇵 and ❤️ love

encode.name: zwj
encode.why: ZWJ sequence (one grapheme is several code points — symbols start at **code point** granularity)

encode.name: combining
encode.why: combining characters — NFC is not applied (applying it changes the id sequence)

encode.name: thai
encode.why: Thai with combining characters (in-vocabulary tokens and byte fallback mix)
encode.text: กำลังทดสอบ

encode.name: control-bytes
encode.why: control characters — not in the vocabulary, they fall to byte_fallback (multi-byte runs included)

encode.name: metaspace-literal
encode.why: U+2581 directly in the input (the character normalization outputs is there from the start)

encode.name: empty
encode.why: the empty string (zero symbols — the initial state of the scan)

encode.name: single-space
encode.why: a single space only (one metaspace character after normalization)

encode.name: prompt-query
encode.why: the prompt prefix 'task: search result | query: ' of `config_sentence_transformers.json` before English text — the real-world shape `<bos>` prompt text `<eos>`
encode.text: task: search result | query: What is the capital of Japan?

encode.name: prompt-only
encode.why: a prompt prefix with an empty text (the input ends on the prefix's trailing space)

encode.name: gemma4-turn-markup
encode.why: Gemma 4's turn and channel markup is added vocabulary here (cut out before BPE)

encode.name: gemma4-media-markup
encode.why: the image, audio and video markup — added tokens numbered past the vocabulary's end (ids 255999 to 258884)

encode.name: gemma4-tool-markup
encode.why: the tool markup and the escape token `<|"|>` glued to text on both sides

encode.name: specials-in-text
encode.why: `<bos>` / `<eos>` / `<pad>` / `<mask>` inside the text (the post-processor's `<bos>` … `<eos>` doubles the first two; decode skips all four)

encode.name: gemma3-turn-markers
encode.why: `<start_of_turn>` is added vocabulary in the first EmbeddingGemma's tokenizer, not in this one — it falls to BPE here

encode.name: long-past-window
encode.why: a document of at least 600 tokens with `<bos>` … `<eos>` — past the 512-position sliding window, where a length limit or a quadratic scan would show

decode.name: byte-run-valid
decode.why: a run that exactly completes a 3-byte character (folded into one character)

decode.name: byte-run-then-token
decode.why: a non-byte token right after an incomplete run (the position where the run's end is settled)

decode.name: byte-run-split-by-token
